Amazon and Tata Motors Partner to Deploy 3,000 Electric Trucks in India Across Key Freight Corridors

30 Oct 2026, 11:22 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Public Services Desk · Source: navbharattimes.indiatimes.com

Key takeaways Overview of the Amazon and Tata Motors Partnership Amazon and Tata Motors have announced a strategic collaboration to introduce 3,000 electric trucks into commercial operations across India. Under this partnership, Tata Motors will supply the electric commercial vehic

Overview of the Amazon and Tata Motors Partnership

Amazon and Tata Motors have announced a strategic collaboration to introduce 3,000 electric trucks into commercial operations across India. Under this partnership, Tata Motors will supply the electric commercial vehicles, while Amazon's carrier partners will manage daily operations. The rollout begins in New Delhi during the peak festive season, focusing on intra-city goods movement.

The initiative aims to transition logistics beyond last-mile delivery into mid-mile and inter-city freight transportation. To support the deployment, Delhi's upcoming electric vehicle policy provisions for the first 1,000 registered medium-duty electric trucks to operate without standard entry restrictions in the city for a 10-year period, aiding supply chain efficiency.

The 2,800 km NH48 Electrified Freight Corridor

Following the urban rollout, the partnership targets the expansion of electric mobility along major national highway infrastructure. The plan includes electrifying a 2,800-kilometer freight corridor along National Highway 48 (NH48), connecting Delhi, Bengaluru, and Chennai.

This interstate route spans seven states and links six major e-commerce hubs. To maintain reliable transit, dedicated electric vehicle charging hubs are being established in collaboration with charging infrastructure provider Yahhvi.

Vehicle Specifications: Tata Ultra E.7

The deployment utilizes the Tata Ultra E.7 electric truck, engineered specifically for logistics operations. Key technical features highlighted in the announcement include:

  • Integrated e-axle technology
  • CCS2 fast-charging capability
  • Regenerative braking systems
  • Crash-tested safety cabins equipped with high-voltage safety cut-off mechanisms

The manufacturer notes that the vehicle is designed to reduce operational costs and maximize uptime compared to traditional diesel-powered equivalents.

Practical Implications and Reader Verification

What is Confirmed

  • Tata Motors will supply 3,000 electric trucks to Amazon's carrier network.
  • Operations commence with intra-city deliveries in Delhi, expanding to a 2,800 km corridor along NH48 connecting Delhi, Bengaluru, and Chennai.
  • The rollout utilizes the Tata Ultra E.7 model with CCS2 fast-charging support.
  • Charging infrastructure along the highway corridor is developed alongside Yahhvi.

What Remains Unknown

  • Specific timelines for the complete delivery of all 3,000 vehicles.
  • Detailed financial terms, capital investments, or commercial valuations of the partnership.
  • Exact locations and operational capacities of all planned charging hubs beyond the initial corridor framework.
